title: Tokyo Drugstore Painkiller and Symptom Guide
yt_title: [JLPT N5] EP.16 Tokyo Drugstore Survival! Buying Painkillers and Explaining Symptoms

cover.jp_line2: よく効く痛み止めありますか？
cover.grammar_tag: JLPT N5 Grammar: Noun がする (Expressing Physical Symptoms & Sensations)
cover.translation: 'I have a bad headache, do you have effective painkillers?'

slides.spoken_text: 頭痛がひどいので、よく効く痛み止めはありますか？
slides.meaning: I have a severe headache, do you have an effective painkiller?
slides.tip: Use '〜がひどい' (is severe) to clearly communicate pain intensity to pharmacy staff.

slides.sentence_ja: 頭痛がひどいので、よく効く痛み止めはありますか？
slides.grammar_title: Symptom Formula: [Body Part / Symptom] がひどい (Severe Pain)
grammar_bullets: EVE (イブ) for mild headaches, Loxonin (ロキソニン) for fast strong relief.
胃痛 (stomach ache), 発熱 (fever), 喉の痛み (sore throat), 鼻水 (runny nose).
食後に1回2錠 (Take 2 tablets once after meals with water).
Class 1 medications like Loxonin require a registered pharmacist (薬剤師) on duty.

teamwork_cues.speaker: explainer
teamwork_cues.text: Let's learn how to explain your symptoms and buy over-the-counter medicine at Japanese drugstores.

teamwork_cues.speaker: explainer
teamwork_cues.text: Noun: painkiller or pain relief medication.

teamwork_cues.speaker: explainer
teamwork_cues.text: Verb phrase: works effectively and quickly.

teamwork_cues.speaker: explainer
teamwork_cues.text: Noun: taking medicine after finishing meals.

teamwork_cues.speaker: explainer
teamwork_cues.text: Grammar Spotlight: state your symptom clearly with ga hidoi.

shorts.romaji_sentence: Zutsuu ga hidoi node, yoku kiku itami-dome wa arimasu ka?
